column3: A temple complex of the Song dynasty near Taiyuan, built around a spring and shaded by ancient cypress trees, with beautiful clay statues of maids.
A museum of Shanxi's long history, with Jin-state bronzes, Buddhist sculptures and relics of the merchants who made the province rich.
Two Ming pagodas that rise side by side above the roofs of Taiyuan, a symbol of the city.
Noodles shaved with a curved knife from a lump of dough straight into boiling water, each strip thick in the middle and thin at the edges, topped with a savory sauce.
A winter dish of lamb, yam, lotus root and a splash of wine, served hot as a breakfast tonic. It is a Taiyuan tradition.
A dark, mellow vinegar aged for years, a symbol of Shanxi, where cooks add it to everything from noodles to dumplings.
Rolls of oat noodle dough shaped into little baskets and steamed, then eaten with a savory sauce.
Slices of pork quickly fried in oil, then stir-fried with vegetables and vinegar, a Taiyuan classic.
Beef that is cured, simmered and pressed in Pingyao, with a tender texture and a rich flavor, and sold in the old town.
A famous clear baijiu from Shanxi that has been made for about 1,500 years, with a light and clean taste.
The local opera of Shanxi, sung in the local dialect, with strong voices and lively music.
Figures made of colored dough, from animals to opera heroes, a folk craft that is also used for festivals.
Shanxi merchants ran trading houses and early banks across China in the Ming and Qing dynasties, which made the province wealthy.
Giant Buddhist carvings from the fifth century, cut into a sandstone cliff near Datong. Some of the Buddhas are 17 meters high. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
A temple stuck to a cliff face, held up by wooden posts, and it seems to hang in the air. It is about 1,500 years old and blends Buddhism, Taoism and Confucianism.
One of the biggest wooden temples in China, built in the Liao and Jin dynasties, with huge halls and painted clay statues.
A glazed wall in Datong with nine colorful dragons, built in the Ming dynasty and bigger than the one in Beijing.
The oldest and tallest wooden pagoda in China, 67 meters high, built in 1056 with no nails.
One of the Five Sacred Mountains of China, in the north, with temples built into the cliffs.
A cool jelly made from starch, served with chili, vinegar and herbs, a favorite summer snack.
A copper hotpot with a chimney in the center, heated with charcoal, an old Datong way to enjoy a meal in winter.
Daylily buds are dried and used in soups and stir-fries, a Datong specialty with a mild and sweet taste.
A Ming walled town with about 3,000 old buildings, courtyard houses and lanes. It was a center of banking in the Qing dynasty, and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
A Ming wall, about six kilometers around, that you can walk on, with watchtowers at regular intervals.
A temple with about 2,000 painted clay statues, some of the finest Buddhist sculpture in China.
A temple with a wooden hall built in the 10th century, one of the oldest in China.
A cool jelly made from buckwheat, sliced and served with garlic, vinegar and chili, a common Pingyao snack.
Lacquerware that is polished by hand until it shines like a mirror, with painted gold designs, a Pingyao craft.
Piaohao were private banks of Pingyao in the Qing dynasty, which moved money across China by drafts.
A big courtyard mansion of a merchant family, with 313 rooms and many courtyards. A famous film made it known worldwide.
A huge Qing complex of courtyards and carved gates, home of the Wang family, nicknamed the Forbidden City of the Loess Plateau.
A merchant manor with gardens and halls that show how wealthy Shanxi merchants lived.
A round, sweet cake with a crisp, flaky crust and sesame, a Taigu specialty that is carried as a gift.
A waterfall where the Yellow River squeezes into a narrow gorge and plunges. This side belongs to Shanxi.
A temple of the Yuan period with a fine glazed pagoda and old wall paintings.
A hot, peppery soup of lamb organs, eaten with flatbread, a Linfen breakfast.
A tower on the bank of the Yellow River, made famous by a Tang poem that every Chinese child learns.
A Taoist temple with huge, remarkable Yuan-dynasty wall paintings of hundreds of immortals.
A salt lake that turns pink in summer, due to algae and minerals, and has been a source of salt for thousands of years.
A lamb soup with torn bread, much like the one in Xi'an, in a local style.
Fried dough twists from Jishan, crisp and sweet, sold as snacks and gifts.
Deep gorges in the Taihang Mountains, with red cliffs, waterfalls and paths that cling to the rock.
A local liquor of Changzhi with a history of centuries.
A walled mansion of a Qing official with many courtyards and watchtowers, a showpiece of old Shanxi architecture.
A local breed of black pig, known for its tender meat and rich flavor.
Sweet red dates grown along the Yellow River in Lüliang, eaten fresh or dried.
A cool jelly made from starch, topped with a spicy sauce, a local version of the snack.
One of the four sacred Buddhist mountains, dedicated to Manjushri, with dozens of temples among its five flat peaks. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
A small Tang-dynasty hall, from 782 CE, the oldest surviving wooden building in China.
A frontier pass on the Great Wall, set in the hills and a gate to the north, with strong walls.
A flaky pastry shaped like roof tiles, which are crisp and sweet.
A big baked flatbread, thick and crunchy, that was a travelers' food, and is still liked as a snack.
